newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 19.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 19. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto said the government should be prepared to make bitter decisions and withdraw democratic rights if it is clear that democracy is being misused to destroy the state and democracy itself.

Bank Indonesia Governor Soedradjad Djiwandono said the country deserved to be happy about the lower inflation rate in 1996 but the nation could not afford to relax its guard as the current account deficit was still a concern.
Senior activists of the controversial Independent Election Monitoring Committee (KIPP) have called on the government to officially recognised the body ahead of next year's general election.
Environmentalists have urged the government to put into practice their political committment to control industrial pollution.
Police in Yogyakarta have freed their key suspect in the killing of a local journalist after strong criticism from human rights bodies and journalists that they had arrested the wrong man.
President Suharto has given his approval to a multi-billion dollar satellite city project outside of Jakarta as proposed by a consortium that includes one of his son's Bambang Trihatmodjo.
